Item0000000003.description: energy balance model coupling global mean surface temperature to a stochastic delay equation for atmospheric CO2
Item0000000003.label: stochastic temperature–CO2 energy balance model

descriptions.en: energy balance model coupling global mean surface temperature to a stochastic delay equation for atmospheric CO2

value.content: Mathematical model for the global mean surface temperature and the atmospheric CO2 concentration, introduced to study climate tipping points under emission reduction and carbon capture scenarios. The temperature follows a Budyko–Sellers-type energy balance: incoming short-wave radiation with a temperature-dependent albedo (a smooth transition between an ice-covered and an ice-free value), greenhouse forcing, and outgoing long-wave radiation, driven by additive white noise. The CO2 concentration follows a stochastic delay differential equation with a time-dependent emission rate as source, a constant carbon capture rate acting with a time delay as sink, and additive white noise. The coupling is one-way: CO2 drives temperature through the greenhouse forcing.

The CO2 concentration follows a stochastic delay differential equation with a time-dependent emission rate as source, a constant carbon capture rate acting with a time delay as sink, and additive white noise. The coupling is one-way: CO2 drives temperature through the greenhouse forcing.

Item0000000004.description: Budyko–Sellers-type stochastic differential equation with temperature-dependent albedo and logarithmic CO2 forcing
Item0000000004.label: stochastic energy balance equation for the global mean surface temperature

descriptions.en: Budyko–Sellers-type stochastic differential equation with temperature-dependent albedo and logarithmic CO2 forcing

labels.en: stochastic energy balance equation for the global mean surface temperature

value.content: Stochastic differential equation for the evolution of the global mean temperature: the thermal inertia times the change of temperature equals the net energy flux, that is the short-wave solar radiation absorbed by the Earth after reflection by the temperature-dependent albedo, plus the trapping of outgoing radiation by greenhouse gases and the logarithmic forcing by the CO2 concentration relative to its preindustrial level, minus the outgoing long-wave radiation modified by the emissivity, plus a stochastic forcing by a Wiener process that represents unresolved subgrid processes.

Item0000000005.description: stochastic delay differential equation with time-dependent emission and delayed carbon capture
Item0000000005.label: stochastic delay equation for the atmospheric CO2 concentration

descriptions.en: stochastic delay differential equation with time-dependent emission and delayed carbon capture

labels.en: stochastic delay equation for the atmospheric CO2 concentration

value.content: Stochastic delay differential equation for the evolution of the atmospheric CO2 concentration: its change is the emission into the atmosphere, proportional to the current concentration with a time-dependent emission rate, minus the capture of CO2 from the atmosphere by natural processes or technologies, proportional to the concentration one delay earlier with a constant carbon capture rate, plus a stochastic forcing by a Wiener process that represents the uncertainties of the concentration.

statements: Stochastic delay differential equation for the evolution of the atmospheric CO2 concentration: its change is the emission into the atmosphere, proportional to the current concentration with a time-dependent emission rate, minus the capture of CO2 from the atmosphere by natural processes or technologies, proportional to the concentration one delay earlier with a constant carbon capture rate, plus a stochastic forcing by a Wiener process that represents the uncertainties of the concentration.

Item0000000008.description: numerical integration of the coupled stochastic delay equations for temperature and CO2 over 200 years under prescribed emission reduction scenarios
Item0000000008.label: simulation of emission reduction scenarios in the stochastic temperature–CO2 model

descriptions.en: numerical integration of the coupled stochastic delay equations for temperature and CO2 over 200 years under prescribed emission reduction scenarios

labels.en: simulation of emission reduction scenarios in the stochastic temperature–CO2 model

value.content: Numerical solution of the initial value problem for the coupled stochastic delay differential equations of the global mean temperature and the atmospheric CO2 concentration. Starting from the current global mean temperature and CO2 concentration, with a constant CO2 history over the preceding delay interval, the system is simulated over a long time span for a range of emission reduction scenarios, given by the terminal emission rate and the time to reach it, to determine whether the CO2 concentration exceeds the critical threshold beyond which the temperature tips into the warm regime.

value.content: Delay differential equation for the evolution of the atmospheric CO2 concentration, obtained from the stochastic delay differential equation by neglecting the stochastic term: the change of the concentration is the emission into the atmosphere, proportional to the current concentration with a time-dependent emission rate, minus the capture of CO2, proportional to the concentration one delay earlier with a constant carbon capture rate. Without the noise, it allows an upper bound for the CO2 concentration to be derived analytically, which determines whether an emission reduction and carbon capture scenario keeps the concentration below the critical threshold of the climate tipping point; the noise only adds small fluctuations around this bound.
